# Strategy-layer plan: `entire://` remote as the home of checkpoint data

All paths are under `/home/toby/projects/cli/cmd/entire/cli/` unless stated. Line numbers are from the files as read today.

## Verified facts the design rests on

- Election lives in `strategy/checkpoint_sync_remote.go:73-112` (`ResolveCheckpointSyncRemote`): config → captured (`loadCapturedSyncRemotes`, fail-soft) → origin → sole → first. Remote listing is `readRemotesInConfigOrder` (`:230-260`), which already runs `git config --local --get-regexp '^remote\..*\.url$'` and throws away the URL after `strings.Cut(line, " ")` at `:248`.
- The per-process cache (`strategy/git_remote_cache.go`) memoizes exactly two reads: the ordered list (`remoteSnapshot.ordered []string`, `:68`) and `isConfiguredRemote` membership (`member`, `:76`). `isConfiguredRemote` (`manual_commit_push.go:360-382`) uses `git remote get-url`, which per git-remote(1) *expands* `url.<base>.insteadOf`; `git config --get-regexp` returns the raw value. That asymmetry is exactly what lets integration tests simulate `entire://` (the trick is already in use at `integration_test/enable_checkpoint_remote_test.go:139-145`: `git config --add url.file:///bare.insteadOf <derived-url>`).
- `captureEligible` (`strategy/checkpoint_sync_capture.go:146-167`) switches on `elected.Source` with an `exhaustive`-linted switch (`.golangci.yaml:25` enables `exhaustive`); a new constant will not compile until it is placed in a case.
- `prePush` (`strategy/manual_commit_push.go:56-226`): gate at `:98-107`, git-refs branch at `:115-117`, empty-remote defer at `:122`, policy sync at `:132`, OPF rewrite with `ps.pushTarget()` at `:169`, v1 push loop with `ps.pushTarget()` at `:200`, capture commit at `:220-222` and (refs path) `:441-443`.
- `pushSettings` (`strategy/checkpoint_remote.go:36-64`): `pushTarget()` returns `checkpointURL` else `remote`.
- `remote.PushWithOptions` (`checkpoint/remote/git.go:428-449`) builds `push --no-verify --porcelain <ExtraArgs...> <target> <refspecs...>`, so `ExtraArgs: []string{"--delete"}` lands before the remote — a valid `git push --delete <remote> <ref>...` invocation, and `--no-verify` is already present. BUT `resolvePushCommandTarget` (`:726-739`) rewrites a remote *name* to the dedicated `checkpoint_remote` URL when one is configured — a hazard for the delete step (see D6).
- `remote.LsRemoteInDir` (`:452`), `remote.Fetch` (`:239`, supports `Dir`, `NoFilter`, `NoTags`, `RefSpecs`).
- `SafelyAdvanceLocalRef` (`strategy/common.go:162-203`): missing/behind → set; equal/ahead → no-op; diverged → replay. `PromoteTmpRefSafely` (`:138-154`) wraps it but re-opens the repo from cwd.
- `checkpoint.MigrateBranchToRefs` (`checkpoint/migrate.go:48`): idempotent via `treeInRefHistory` (`:104`, `:148`), enqueues every checkpoint including already-imported ones (`:118`, `:167`), and its "no branch" path (`:65-68`) reads through `getSessionsBranchTree`, which can fall back to the origin tracking ref — so it must run *after* hydration. Tests `migrate_test.go:207` and `:452` prove re-runs do not regress a ref advanced past the snapshot.
- `PushQueue.Enqueue` (`checkpoint/pushqueue.go:83-103`) appends under flock; `Drain` (`:115-132`) dedups and compacts. `PushQueuedCheckpointRefs` (`manual_commit_push.go:464-488`) → `flushCheckpointRefsQueue` (`:498-600`) → `batchPushRefs` (`push_common.go:58-70`) pushes *every* queued ref in one argv.
- `parseCheckpointRefNames` is in package `cli` (`git_operations.go:707-721`); `checkpoint` and `checkpoint/remote` do not import each other in either direction (verified by grep), and `CheckpointRefPrefix` lives in `checkpoint/refs_naming.go:16`.
- `deleteBranchFromRemote` (`trail_cmd.go:2590-2602`) treats `remote ref does not exist` as success.
- `EnsureRedactionConfigured` precondition for any queue flush: documented at `manual_commit_push.go:255-265`, honored by `doctor_migrate.go:123`.
- Status vocabulary: `status.go:406-410` renders `config`/`observed`; JSON comment at `status.go:810` enumerates `config|observed|default|sole|first|dedicated`.
- CLAUDE.md `EnvWithoutRepoOverrides` rule (`CLAUDE.md:1160-1166`): applies to subprocesses that can run inside a hook and target via `cmd.Dir`/`-C`; "deliberately not applied to user-invoked commands that act on the current directory".
- `git-remote-entire` (`cmd/git-remote-entire/main.go`) is a transport proxy (stateless-connect over smart HTTP); it has no ref filtering of its own — the "mirror does not forward refs/entire/* to GitHub" property is a server-side product decision, taken as given.

---

## A. Entire-remote detection

### A1. `gitremote.IsEntireURL` — `gitremote/gitremote.go`
```go
// IsEntireURL reports whether raw names Entire's git remote helper. A scheme
// prefix check, not ParseURL: git itself picks the helper from "<scheme>://",
// and a URL whose path ParseURL cannot split into owner/repo is still an
// entire:// remote as far as transport is concerned.
func IsEntireURL(raw string) bool
```
Implementation: `strings.HasPrefix(strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(raw)), ProtocolEntire+"://")`. Sits next to `ProtocolEntire` (`:21`). Unit test in `gitremote_test.go` (entire://, ENTIRE://, https://, scp-style, `entire:` without slashes → false).

### A2. Retain URLs in the config-order read — `strategy/checkpoint_sync_remote.go`
- New type near `:214`:
  ```go
  // configuredRemote is one remote.<name>.url entry set, in .git/config order.
  type configuredRemote struct {
      Name string
      URLs []string // every remote.<name>.url value, config order (git remote get-url --all)
  }
  ```
- Change `readRemotesInConfigOrder(ctx) ([]configuredRemote, error)`: keep the existing parsing loop (`:245-258`) but retain `value` from `strings.Cut` and append to the entry's `URLs` instead of skipping duplicates. Keep the exit-code-1 = "no remotes" contract (`:238-240`) intact — the cache relies on it.
- `configuredRemotesInConfigOrder(ctx) []string` keeps its signature (callers at `:101`, tests) and maps names out of the new `cachedRemotesInConfigOrder` result.
- New `configuredEntireRemotes(ctx) []string`: names whose `URLs` is non-empty and **every** URL satisfies `gitremote.IsEntireURL`. "Every", not "any": a remote with an entire:// fetch url and a GitHub pushurl fans out to GitHub, and the tier must never elect a destination that can leak transcripts to a non-Entire mirror. Note: pushurl is deliberately not consulted (same "pushurl-only remotes are invisible" rule as `:216-217`); a remote with `url=entire://…` and `pushurl=https://github.com/…` would still be elected by this rule — flag as **D1** below; the safe option is to also read `^remote\..*\.pushurl$` in the same regexp (`'^remote\..*\.(url|pushurl)$'`) and require every pushurl to be entire:// too. I recommend the safe option; it costs nothing (same subprocess).

### A3. Cache changes — `strategy/git_remote_cache.go`
- `remoteSnapshot.ordered` becomes `[]configuredRemote` (`:68`); `cachedRemotesInConfigOrder`'s `read` parameter and return become `[]configuredRemote` (`:178`). Doc at `:11-24` gains one sentence: the list now carries raw URLs so the entire-remote tier costs no extra subprocess. Nothing else changes; `member` stays separate because it answers a different question (`:70-75`).

### A4. Why raw config, restated for the code comment
`git remote get-url` expands `insteadOf`; raw config does not. Production repos have `entire://` in raw config and the helper does transport. Tests put `entire://cluster.test/gh/o/r` in raw config plus `url.file:///…/bare.insteadOf entire://cluster.test/gh/o/r`, so raw says entire:// and every `git fetch/push/ls-remote <name>` goes to the bare. TestEnv's `.git/config` guard (`integration_test/testenv.go:249-285`) compares snapshots, so tests must call `env.setGitConfigBaseline()` after adding the insteadOf key (same as `setBranchTrackingRemote` does at `checkpoint_sync_remote_test.go:121`).

---

## B. Election tier and vocabulary

### B1. Constant — `strategy/checkpoint_sync_remote.go:20-34`

```go
// (Entire's own git remote helper). Checkpoint data belongs on Entire, so it
// outranks the default tiers but not an explicit setting or a capture already

SyncRemoteSourceEntire CheckpointSyncRemoteSource = "entire"
```

### C1. `pushSettings` — `strategy/checkpoint_remote.go:36-64`
```go

// differs from remote: this push was made to some other target, and the
```

```go

// dedicated checkpoint URL is in play and the election elected an entire://
// remote other than the one being pushed, the checkpoint target becomes that
// remote. Returns the election when the entire tier is in force (redirected or
// not) so the caller can announce delivery; ok=false leaves ps untouched and

```

## D. Migration engine — `strategy/checkpoint_sync_migrate.go` (new) + small helpers

### D2. Hydrate
```go
type HydrateResult struct {
    RefsFetched  int   // refs fetched from the old remote
    RefsAdvanced int   // local refs set or fast-forwarded
    RefsReplayed int   // diverged local refs replayed onto the old tip (logged at Info by SafelyAdvanceLocalRef)
    V1Advanced   bool
}
func HydrateCheckpointArtifacts(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, from string, inv CheckpointInventory, progress ProgressFunc) (HydrateResult, error)
```
- Candidates: every `inv.Refs` entry whose local ref is absent **or** whose local hash differs from the remote hash (a ref written on another machine may be ahead on the old remote; deleting it after publishing only the local tip would lose it).
- Fetch in chunks of `refChunkSize` with refspecs `+refs/entire/checkpoints/<s>/<id>:refs/entire-sync-tmp/checkpoints/<s>/<id>` via `remote.Fetch(ctx, remote.FetchOptions{Remote: from, RefSpecs, NoTags: true, NoFilter: true, Dir: worktreeRoot})`. `NoFilter: true` is mandatory — see the doc at `checkpoint_remote.go:169-181`: filtered fetches leave refs whose blobs are missing, and the ref's existence then suppresses recovery forever.
- Promote each tmp ref with `SafelyAdvanceLocalRef(ctx, repo, localRef, tmpHash)` (`common.go:162`), then `repo.Storer.RemoveReference(tmp)`. Do not use `PromoteTmpRefSafely` (`:138`): it re-opens the repo from cwd; the engine takes an explicit `repo`.
- v1: if `!inv.V1Branch.IsZero()`, fetch `+refs/heads/entire/checkpoints/v1:refs/entire-sync-tmp/heads/entire/checkpoints/v1` (same options) and `SafelyAdvanceLocalRef(ctx, repo, checkpoint.ResolveRefs(ctx).Primary, tmpHash)`.
- **Why this does not violate "only the elected remote may advance local refs"** (CLAUDE.md:1433): that rule protects the automatic read paths from a stale legacy tier silently replaying onto local state during a hook or a resume. Here (1) the user issued a foreground command and consented, (2) the source is the remote *being migrated from*, whose data we are about to delete — hydrating it into local refs is the only thing that makes deletion safe, and (3) promotion goes through the same non-destructive `SafelyAdvanceLocalRef` (ahead → untouched, diverged → replay + Info log). The tmp namespace keeps the fetch itself from ever writing a canonical ref directly, matching the `fetchURLIntoTmpRef` + promote shape the codebase already uses (`checkpoint_remote.go:143-160`). Document this in the function comment and reference the CLAUDE.md rule.

### D3. Convert
Engine exposes nothing new: the CLI calls `checkpoint.MigrateBranchToRefs(ctx, repo, false)` after D2 when the local v1 branch exists (`repo.Reference(checkpoint.ResolveRefs(ctx).Primary, true)` succeeds). Idempotency verified (`migrate.go:104,148`; tests `:207`, `:452`). It enqueues every checkpoint — which is exactly the D4 requeue for the converted set. Ordering constraint: hydrate → convert → **backend flip** (`applyCheckpointBackend`, `checkpoint_backend.go:61`, CLI half) → requeue+publish → verify → remove. The flip must precede publish so `CountUnpushedCheckpoints`/status read the queue, and must precede the user's next `git push` so the pre-push takes the refs path (`primaryIsRefs`, `manual_commit_push.go:115`). Note `doctor migrate-checkpoints` refuses when refs is already primary (`doctor_migrate.go:46-49`); `MigrateBranchToRefs` itself does not, so the new command can convert first and flip after.

### D6. Remove
```go
type RemoveResult struct{ RefsDeleted int; V1Deleted bool; AlreadyAbsent int }
func RemoveCheckpointArtifacts(ctx context.Context, oldRemote string, refs []plumbing.ReferenceName, deleteV1 bool, progress ProgressFunc) (RemoveResult, error)
```
- Shared helper in `checkpoint/remote/git.go`:
  ```go
  // DeleteRefs runs `git push --no-verify --porcelain --delete <target> <refs...>`.
  // A ref that is already absent is reported in absent rather than failing the call.
  func DeleteRefs(ctx context.Context, target, dir string, refs []string) (absent []string, err error)
  ```
  built on `PushWithOptions{Remote: target, ExtraArgs: []string{"--delete"}, RefSpecs: refs, Dir: dir}` (`:428-449`). Git validates `--delete` refspecs before transferring, so one absent ref fails the whole invocation with `remote ref does not exist`; on that error `DeleteRefs` re-runs `ls-remote` for the chunk, drops the absent names, and retries once. Generalize `deleteBranchFromRemote` (`trail_cmd.go:2590`) to call it with one ref (behavior preserved: absent → nil).
- **Target must be the old remote's URL, not its name.** `resolvePushCommandTarget` (`git.go:726-739`) rewrites a remote *name* to the dedicated `checkpoint_remote` `PushURL` when one is configured — a `--delete` aimed at "origin" would then delete from the dedicated checkpoint repo. Resolve with `gitremote.GetPushURLs(ctx, oldRemote)` (`gitremote.go:156`) and refuse (`error`) when it returns more than one URL (a fan-out remote has no single "old" to clean). `IsURL`/`isLocalPath` targets bypass the rewrite (`:727`). Belt and braces: the CLI should also refuse the whole command when `settings.GetCheckpointRemote() != nil` (a dedicated store is authoritative; this feature is about the default election) — **open question D6**.
- Chunk at `refChunkSize`; only refs in `verified` are ever passed in.
- v1: `DeleteRefs(ctx, url, dir, []string{"refs/heads/"+paths.MetadataBranchName})` when `deleteV1`. Then prune the stale local tracking ref `refs/remotes/<old>/entire/checkpoints/v1` (`repo.Storer.RemoveReference`); otherwise `metadataTrackingRefExists` (`git_operations.go:464-471`) and `countUnpushedV1Commits` (`unpushed_checkpoints.go:58`) keep seeing a branch the remote no longer has.
- `EnvWithoutRepoOverrides`: **not required**. The rule (CLAUDE.md:1160-1166) targets subprocesses that can run inside a git hook; this engine runs only from a foreground command in the user's cwd, where an exported `GIT_DIR` is an instruction. Say so in the file header, and note that if any of these functions is ever wired into a hook, `remote.Fetch/PushWithOptions` do not scrub the environment (`newCommand`, `git.go:544-557`).

### D7. Legacy read tier after removal
`CheckpointReadRemotesWithElection` (`checkpoint_read_remotes.go:58-74`) yields `[entire, origin]`. After removal: `ListCheckpointRefsOnRemote` unions per-candidate listings (`git_operations.go:662-697`) — origin contributes nothing, fine. `FetchCheckpointRefFrom` (`checkpoint_ref.go:219-296`) asks the entire remote first (authoritative via `LeadReadRemote` → `fetchURLAuthoritative`, `util.go:113-124`), falls to origin only on positive absence, and returns `ErrReferenceNotFound` on absence everywhere; nothing persists an "absent" verdict across processes. The git-refs store's per-process failure memo is scoped to one process. The checkpoint policy ref `refs/entire/policies/checkpoint` (`checkpointpolicy/store.go:22`) on origin is left alone (harmless, read-only tier; the hook writes the policy to `pushTarget()`, which is now the entire remote). The election cache (`git_remote_cache.go`) memoizes only `.git/config` reads; the CLI half must call `strategy.InvalidateGitRemoteCache(ctx)` if it adds or renames a remote (e.g. `--to` accepting a URL).

### D8. Ordering constraints (engine-level)
1. Inventory(old) → 2. Hydrate(old) → 3. Convert (if local v1) → 4. *CLI flips backend* → 5. RequeueAll → EnsureRedactionConfigured → PushQueuedCheckpointRefs(new) → 6. Verify(new, old inventory) → 7. Remove(old, verified only) → 8. `MarkEntireSyncMigration(done|declined, old)`. If step 5 pushes 0 with `pushDisabled` (`push_sessions: false`), the CLI must stop before 7.

## Risks and open questions

- **D1** pushurl: adopt the safe rule (read `(url|pushurl)`, require all entire://)? Recommended yes.
- **D2** (the recommendation in C): redirect ANY push to the entire remote. Consequence worth stating: a user with `remote.pushDefault=github` never pushes to `entire` yet checkpoints go there on every push, and the SSH/auth for the entire helper runs inside every `git push`. Helper auth failure is fail-soft for refs (`:444-449`) but the v1 path's `doPushRef` is fail-soft too; `BatchMode` SSH does not apply (HTTPS helper). Fine, but the first-push latency is new.
- **D3** skip the empty-remote defer under redirect: relies on Entire never adopting `entire/checkpoints/v1` as the mirror's HEAD. Needs server-side confirmation.
- **D4** captured tier outranks entire: a repo that captured `origin`/`fork` before adding the Entire remote never reaches the tier. Options: (a) leave, and have `entire checkpoint sync --to <entire>` clear the capture file (expose `ClearCapturedSyncRemote(ctx) error` in `checkpoint_sync_capture.go`), or (b) place the entire tier above captured. The product order given says (a); recommend exposing the clear helper so the CLI can make the election land on `entire` without writing `checkpoint_push_remote`.
- **D5** `checkpoint_remote` configured *and* an entire remote: `hasCheckpointURL()` still wins in `prePush` (`:99`), so dedicated mode is unaffected and the entire tier is irrelevant there. Should `entire status` say so? Current `computeCheckpointSyncInfo` probes `PushURL(elected.Name)` with an entire:// elected remote (`util.go:312-324` provider fallback) — same as today for any remote.
- **D6** the delete step must never reach a `checkpoint_remote`: engine resolves the old remote to its URL (bypasses `resolvePushCommandTarget`) and the CLI refuses when `checkpoint_remote` is set.
- **Ref-per-push argv limits**: pre-existing latent bug in `batchPushRefs`; the backlog publish makes it real. Chunking is part of this plan.
- **Hydration cost**: an old remote with thousands of checkpoint refs is fetched with blobs (`NoFilter`); budget is per chunk under `migrateRemoteTimeout`, and the CLI should show progress.
- **Concurrency**: a `git push` pre-push hook running mid-migration flushes the same queue; `flushCheckpointRefsQueue` removes only landed refs, so both drain safely to the same elected remote. The remove step only deletes verified refs, so a concurrent hook cannot cause loss.

- `Long` (human reference, no agent guidance):

```
Choose the one git remote that carries this repository's checkpoints and bring
the backlog over to it.

When one of your remotes is an Entire remote (entire://…), it is the destination:
Entire keeps checkpoints alongside your code, and pushes to an Entire mirror stay
on Entire rather than being forwarded to the upstream forge. Otherwise pass --to
to pick a remote; the choice is recorded in .entire/settings.local.json as
strategy_options.checkpoint_push_remote, because a remote name is a fact about
this clone, not about the project.

What sync does, in order, skipping steps that are already done:
  1. Convert git-branch checkpoints (entire/checkpoints/v1) to per-checkpoint
     refs and make git-refs the primary store.
  2. Fetch checkpoint artifacts that exist only on the old remote.
  3. Push every checkpoint ref to the destination and verify it arrived.
  4. With your consent (--remove, or a prompt), delete the checkpoint refs and
     the entire/checkpoints/v1 branch from the old remote. Your code is never
     touched.

Without a terminal, sync reports the plan and the exact command to run; it
writes nothing unless --yes is passed, and deletes nothing unless --remove is.
```

### 2.2 Decision order (pure)

1. `len(in.Remotes) == 0` → `no_remotes`, Reason `This repo has no git remotes, so there is nowhere to sync checkpoints to. Add one with git remote add, then rerun.` exit 0.
2. `in.DedicatedRemote` → `dedicated_remote` (h). Stop.
3. `in.ElectionErr != nil` and `Opts.To == ""` → `fail_closed` (g), exit 1. With `--to` valid → continue with `Destination = Opts.To`, `WriteDestinationSetting = true`.
4. Destination resolution:
   - `Opts.To != ""`: must be a configured remote (else `ExitError: --to %q is not a configured git remote`). `WriteDestinationSetting = Elected.Name != Opts.To || ElectionErr != nil`. Source `"flag"` (or the election source if it already matches).
   - else `len(EntireRemotes) >= 2` and elected source is not config/observed → `choose_destination` (f). Interactive: picker; non-interactive: `ExitError: several Entire remotes (%s); pass --to <remote>`.
   - else `Elected.Source == SyncRemoteSourceEntire` → Destination = Elected.Name, source `entire`.
   - else `len(EntireRemotes) == 0` and `len(Remotes) > 1` and source is default/sole/first → `choose_destination` (b). Interactive: picker with current election first; non-interactive: Reason + `entire checkpoint sync --to <remote>` and settings advice, exit 0 (it is advisory, nothing is broken; mirrors doctor REVIEW).
   - else Destination = Elected.Name (single remote, or config/observed).
5. `--from` validation: every name must be configured and `!= Destination`; else `ExitError`.
6. Sources: `Opts.From` if given, else every non-destination remote whose `Inventory.holdsArtifacts()`; inventory errors go to `UnknownSources`. Decision for several holders: **migrate from all** (hydrate is a union; there is no "wrong" data to bring, and leaving artifacts on any remote defeats the durability goal). Removal stays per-remote with its own confirmation and URL. `--from` narrows when the user wants otherwise.
7. Steps:
   - `!PrimaryIsRefs` → `convert_backend` (i). Skip writing when `BackendEnvOverride`.
   - each Source → `hydrate`.
   - `PrimaryIsRefs && QueuedRefs == 0 && LocalCheckpoints > 0` → `requeue` (already-pushed refs are no longer queued; migration re-enqueues on its own, `migrate.go:117-123,167`).
   - `publish`, `verify` always when `LocalCheckpoints > 0 || len(Sources) > 0`.
   - `remove` when `len(Sources) > 0` (consent gathered at run time; the planner only says it is on the table).
   - `record_marker` always at the end.
8. State assignment: `WriteDestinationSetting`-only with zero checkpoints and no sources → `set_destination` (e); no sources and `LocalCheckpoints > 0` and (`QueuedRefs > 0` or destination inventory lacks refs) → `publish_only` (d); no sources, refs all present on destination (destination inventory ⊇ local refs) → `already_home` (a/n); otherwise `migrate` (c/i).
9. `PushSessionsDisabled` (l) does not change the state; it adds `Reason` suffix and the executor knows `Push` will report `pushDisabled`.

### 2.4 Old-remote auto-detection rule

Preference for messaging (which remote is "the old one" in prose and in the status nudge): `legacyElectedRemote(in)` = `origin` if configured and not entire, else the sole non-entire remote, else the first non-entire remote in config order — the election without the entire tier. For *action*, every non-destination remote whose inventory holds artifacts is a source (Section 2.2 step 6). Non-interactive `--remove` applies to all sources; `--from` narrows. Justification: hydrating from all is monotone (more data, never less); removal is the only irreversible act and it stays per-remote with its own consent line naming the URL.

### 3.2 Step lines (spinner then `✓`)

# Checkpoints find their home on Entire: `entire checkpoint sync`

## Context

A repo with more than one git remote today prints, at `entire enable` and `entire doctor`
(`cmd/entire/cli/remote_topology.go:177-178`), the advice "set `checkpoint_remote` in
`.entire/settings.json`". That advice is wrong twice over: `checkpoint_remote` is a
`{"provider","repo"}` object naming a *dedicated GitHub checkpoint repository*
(`settings/settings.go:1886`), not a remote picker, and a string placed under it is
silently ignored. The knob that actually selects which configured remote carries
checkpoints is `strategy_options.checkpoint_push_remote`, read only by
`ResolveCheckpointSyncRemote` (`strategy/checkpoint_sync_remote.go:73`), and it belongs
in `.entire/settings.local.json` (a remote name is per-clone; see the rationale at
`checkpoint_sync_remote.go:155-158`). The same wrong advice is in
`strategy/refs_push_destination.go:116`. No test covers either string.

Entire's own `entire://` remote (served by `git-remote-entire`) is the store optimized for
checkpoint data, and pushes of `refs/entire/*` / `entire/checkpoints/v1` to an `entire://`
mirror stay on Entire (they are not forwarded to GitHub). So when one of a repo's remotes
is `entire://`, the right outcome is: checkpoints sync there, the backlog already on the
other remote is brought over, and (with consent) the copies on the other remote are
removed. The moment that completes should feel rewarding and show the value the user has
accumulated.

## Decisions

Confirmed with the user:

| # | Decision |
| --- | --- |
| D1 | Command surface is `entire checkpoint sync` with a full non-interactive form (`--to`, `--from`, `--remove`, `--yes`, `--dry-run`, `--json`). |
| D2 | New election tier: a **sole** `entire://` remote is auto-elected after `config` and `observed`, before `origin`/sole/first. Source `SyncRemoteSourceEntire = "entire"`. |
| D3 | Scope: git-refs natively; git-branch repos are first **converted to git-refs** (existing `checkpoint.MigrateBranchToRefs`) and the primary flipped, then published to Entire. Dedicated `checkpoint_remote` repos are out of scope (explained, not migrated). |
| D4 | Removal from the old remote is opt-in, happens only after ls-remote verification that every artifact is on the Entire remote at the local hash, and is never implied by a bare non-interactive run. |

Recommended, adopted in this plan, flagged for the user:

| # | Recommendation | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1 | When the elected sync remote is `entire://`, **every** `git push <any remote or raw URL>` carries checkpoints to the Entire remote (by remote name), the way the dedicated `checkpoint_remote` URL mode already bypasses the single-remote gate (`manual_commit_push.go:99`). | After D2 flips the election, a user whose habit is `git push origin` (GitHub) would otherwise strand checkpoints locally forever. An Entire remote is not a leak surface, which is the only reason the gate exists. |
| R2 | `--to` writes `checkpoint_push_remote` to `.entire/settings.local.json` **only** when the election would not already pick that remote. | Writing it when the tier already elects the remote adds a per-clone setting for nothing and fail-closes anyone who later commits the file. |
| R3 | Detection reads **raw** `.git/config` URLs (`remote.<n>.url` **and** `remote.<n>.pushurl`), and a remote counts as Entire only when every URL is `entire://`. | `git remote get-url` expands `url.<base>.insteadOf`; raw config does not. A remote with an `entire://` url and a GitHub pushurl fans out to GitHub and must not be elected. Raw reads also enable the integration-test trick below. |
| R4 | Under R1 the git-branch "empty remote defer" (`deferCheckpointPushOnEmptyRemote`) is skipped when the push was redirected to the Entire remote. | Keying it on the Entire remote's tracking refs would defer v1 forever for a user who never pushes code to it. Assumes the Entire server never adopts `entire/checkpoints/v1` as a mirror's default branch. |
| R5 | `entire enable` prints a pointer to the command, not an inline migration. Web link omitted from the celebration. | Enable is already three prompts long and must stay offline-tolerant; inventory needs `ls-remote`. No repo-landing web URL is verified in this codebase (trail and experts builders disagree on the path shape). |

## Verified facts the design rests on

### 1.4 Migration engine: new `strategy/checkpoint_sync_migrate.go`

File header states: runs only from a foreground command, so `gitrepo.EnvWithoutRepoOverrides` is deliberately not applied (CLAUDE.md rule targets hook subprocesses); if ever wired into a hook, `remote.Fetch/PushWithOptions` do not scrub the environment.

```go
type ProgressFunc func(format string, args ...any)
type CheckpointInventory struct {
    Remote   string
    Refs     map[plumbing.ReferenceName]plumbing.Hash // refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<id>
    V1Branch plumbing.Hash                            // zero when absent
}
const migrateRemoteTimeout = checkpointRemoteForegroundFetchTimeout // 2 min per network step
const refChunkSize = 200                                            // refspecs per git invocation

func InventoryCheckpointArtifacts(ctx, remoteName string) (CheckpointInventory, error)
func HydrateCheckpointArtifacts(ctx, repo, from string, inv CheckpointInventory, progress ProgressFunc) (HydrateResult, error)
func RequeueAllCheckpointRefs(ctx, repo) (int, error)
func VerifyCheckpointArtifacts(ctx, repo, newRemote string, expected []plumbing.ReferenceName) (verified, missing []plumbing.ReferenceName, err error)
func RemoveCheckpointArtifacts(ctx, oldRemote string, refs []plumbing.ReferenceName, deleteV1 bool, progress ProgressFunc) (RemoveResult, error)
```

1. **Inventory**: `remote.LsRemoteInDir(ctx, worktreeRoot, remoteName, checkpoint.CheckpointRefPrefix+"*", "refs/heads/"+paths.MetadataBranchName)` by remote **name** (git applies insteadOf and dispatches the helper) under `migrateRemoteTimeout`. Move the parser into `checkpoint/refs_naming.go` as `ParseLsRemoteRefs(output) map[plumbing.ReferenceName]plumbing.Hash` plus `ParseCheckpointRefNames`; make `cli.parseCheckpointRefNames` a delegate.
2. **Hydrate**: candidates are inventory refs absent locally or at a different hash. Fetch in chunks with `remote.Fetch{Remote: from, RefSpecs: "+<ref>:refs/entire-sync-tmp/…", NoTags: true, NoFilter: true}` (NoFilter is mandatory, see `checkpoint_remote.go:169-181`), promote each with `SafelyAdvanceLocalRef` (not `PromoteTmpRefSafely`, which reopens the repo from cwd), remove the tmp ref. Same for the v1 branch onto `checkpoint.ResolveRefs(ctx).Primary`. Doc comment explains why this is the one sanctioned non-elected-remote advance: foreground, consented, the source is about to be deleted, and promotion is the same non-destructive primitive.
3. **Convert**: CLI calls `checkpoint.MigrateBranchToRefs(ctx, repo, false)` after hydrate whenever a local v1 branch exists (any backend). Nothing new in strategy.
4. **Requeue + publish**: `RequeueAllCheckpointRefs` iterates `repo.References()` keeping `checkpoint.ParseRef` hits, then `PushQueue.EnqueueAll(refs)` (new, one lock). Publish is existing `EnsureRedactionConfigured` + `PushQueuedCheckpointRefs(ctx, repo, newRemote)`. **Required fix**: chunk `batchPushRefs` at `refChunkSize` (`push_common.go:58-70`). Add `refsPushProgressWriter io.Writer = os.Stderr` (mirroring `opfPrePushProgressWriter`, `manual_commit_push.go:34`) and route the `[entire] Pushing …` line and dots (`:535-536`) through it so the CLI can silence them under its spinner.
5. **Verify**: one ls-remote of the new remote; a ref is verified iff present at the local hash.
6. **Remove**: new `remote.DeleteRefs(ctx, target, dir string, refs []string) (absent []string, err error)` in `checkpoint/remote/git.go` built on `PushWithOptions{ExtraArgs: ["--delete"]}`; on `remote ref does not exist`, re-ls-remote the chunk, drop absent names, retry once. Generalize `trail_cmd.go` `deleteBranchFromRemote` onto it. **Target is the old remote's push URL** (`gitremote.GetPushURLs`), never its name, to bypass `resolvePushCommandTarget`'s dedicated-repo rewrite; refuse a fan-out remote (>1 push URL). Chunk at `refChunkSize`; only verified refs. Delete `refs/heads/entire/checkpoints/v1` when asked and prune the stale local tracking ref `refs/remotes/<old>/entire/checkpoints/v1`.
7. Legacy read tier after removal needs no change: `FetchCheckpointRefFrom` treats the elected remote as authoritative and origin's absence as absence; nothing persists an "absent" verdict.

Engine ordering (CLI enforces): Inventory(old…) → Hydrate(all sources, refs + v1) → Convert (if local v1) → *backend flip* → Requeue → EnsureRedactionConfigured → Publish(new) → Verify(new) → Remove(old, verified only) → `MarkEntireSyncMigration`.

### 2.2 Command

`Use: "sync"`, `Short: "Move checkpoints to a single remote and bring older ones with them"`. Long explains the four steps (convert, fetch, push+verify, remove with consent), that the destination is the Entire remote when there is one, that `--to` records `strategy_options.checkpoint_push_remote` in `.entire/settings.local.json` because a remote name is a per-clone fact, and that without a terminal it reports and writes nothing unless `--yes`, deletes nothing unless `--remove`.

Flags: `--to <remote>`, `--from <remote>` (repeatable), `--remove`, `--yes` (never implies `--remove`), `--dry-run` (network reads only), `--json` (no prompts). `--dry-run` is mutually exclusive with `--remove` and `--yes`.

Runner: gather inputs (settings, election, `strategy.EntireRemotes`, raw remote list, dedicated-mode probe as `status.go:353`, backend + `ENTIRE_CHECKPOINTS_PRIMARY`, local checkpoint count, queue length, `push_sessions`, marker, `CanPromptInteractively`; inventory every non-destination remote and the destination unless the planner short-circuits) → plan → header → non-interactive/JSON without `--yes` prints plan + exact command and returns → execute with confirmations → celebration.

# Checkpoints find their home on Entire: `entire checkpoint sync`

## Context

A repo with more than one git remote today prints, at `entire enable` and `entire doctor`
(`cmd/entire/cli/remote_topology.go:177-178`), the advice "set `checkpoint_remote` in
`.entire/settings.json`". That advice is wrong twice over: `checkpoint_remote` is a
`{"provider","repo"}` object naming a *dedicated GitHub checkpoint repository*
(`settings/settings.go:1886`), not a remote picker, and a string placed under it is
silently ignored. The knob that actually selects which configured remote carries
checkpoints is `strategy_options.checkpoint_push_remote`, read only by
`ResolveCheckpointSyncRemote` (`strategy/checkpoint_sync_remote.go:73`), and it belongs
in `.entire/settings.local.json` (a remote name is per-clone; see the rationale at
`checkpoint_sync_remote.go:155-158`). The same wrong advice is in
`strategy/refs_push_destination.go:116`. No test covers either string.

Entire's own `entire://` remote (served by `git-remote-entire`) is the store optimized for
checkpoint data, and pushes of `refs/entire/*` / `entire/checkpoints/v1` to an `entire://`
mirror stay on Entire (they are not forwarded to GitHub). So when one of a repo's remotes
is `entire://`, the right outcome is: checkpoints sync there, the backlog already on the
other remote is brought over, and (with consent) the copies on the other remote are
removed. The moment that completes should feel rewarding and show the value the user has
accumulated.

## Decisions

Confirmed with the user:

| # | Decision |
| --- | --- |
| D1 | Command surface is `entire checkpoint sync` with a full non-interactive form (`--to`, `--from`, `--remove`, `--yes`, `--dry-run`, `--json`). |
| D2 | New election tier: a **sole** `entire://` remote is auto-elected after `config` and `observed`, before `origin`/sole/first. Source `SyncRemoteSourceEntire = "entire"`. |
| D3 | Scope: git-refs natively; git-branch repos are first **converted to git-refs** (existing `checkpoint.MigrateBranchToRefs`) and the primary flipped, then published to Entire. Dedicated `checkpoint_remote` repos are out of scope (explained, not migrated). |
| D4 | Removal from the old remote is opt-in, happens only after ls-remote verification that every artifact is on the Entire remote at the local hash, and is never implied by a bare non-interactive run. |

Recommended, adopted in this plan, flagged for the user:

| # | Recommendation | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| R1 | When the elected sync remote is `entire://`, **every** `git push <any remote or raw URL>` carries checkpoints to the Entire remote (by remote name), the way the dedicated `checkpoint_remote` URL mode already bypasses the single-remote gate (`manual_commit_push.go:99`). | After D2 flips the election, a user whose habit is `git push origin` (GitHub) would otherwise strand checkpoints locally forever. An Entire remote is not a leak surface, which is the only reason the gate exists. |
| R2 | `--to` writes `checkpoint_push_remote` to `.entire/settings.local.json` **only** when the election would not already pick that remote. | Writing it when the tier already elects the remote adds a per-clone setting for nothing and fail-closes anyone who later commits the file. |
| R3 | Detection reads **raw** `.git/config` URLs (`remote.<n>.url` **and** `remote.<n>.pushurl`), and a remote counts as Entire only when every URL is `entire://`. | `git remote get-url` expands `url.<base>.insteadOf`; raw config does not. A remote with an `entire://` url and a GitHub pushurl fans out to GitHub and must not be elected. Raw reads also enable the integration-test trick below. |
| R4 | Under R1 the git-branch "empty remote defer" (`deferCheckpointPushOnEmptyRemote`) is skipped when the push was redirected to the Entire remote. | Keying it on the Entire remote's tracking refs would defer v1 forever for a user who never pushes code to it. Assumes the Entire server never adopts `entire/checkpoints/v1` as a mirror's default branch. |
| R5 | `entire enable` prints a pointer to the command, not an inline migration. Web link omitted from the celebration. | Enable is already three prompts long and must stay offline-tolerant; inventory needs `ls-remote`. No repo-landing web URL is verified in this codebase (trail and experts builders disagree on the path shape). |

# Checkpoints find their home on Entire: `entire checkpoint sync`

## Context

A repo with more than one git remote today prints, at `entire enable` and `entire doctor`
(`cmd/entire/cli/remote_topology.go:177-178`), the advice "set `checkpoint_remote` in
`.entire/settings.json`". That advice is wrong twice over: `checkpoint_remote` is a
`{"provider","repo"}` object naming a *dedicated GitHub checkpoint repository*
(`settings/settings.go:1886`), not a remote picker, and a string placed under it is
silently ignored. The knob that actually selects which configured remote carries
checkpoints is `strategy_options.checkpoint_push_remote`, read only by
`ResolveCheckpointSyncRemote` (`strategy/checkpoint_sync_remote.go:73`), and it belongs
in `.entire/settings.local.json` (a remote name is per-clone; see the rationale at
`checkpoint_sync_remote.go:155-158`). The same wrong advice is in
`strategy/refs_push_destination.go:116`. No test covers either string.

Entire's own `entire://` remote (served by `git-remote-entire`) is the store optimized for
checkpoint data, and pushes of `refs/entire/*` / `entire/checkpoints/v1` to an `entire://`
mirror stay on Entire (they are not forwarded to GitHub). So when one of a repo's remotes
is `entire://`, the right outcome is: checkpoints sync there, the backlog already on the
other remote is brought over, and (with consent) the copies on the other remote are
removed. The moment that completes should feel rewarding and show the value the user has
accumulated.

## Decisions

Confirmed with the user:

| # | Decision |
| --- | --- |
| D1 | Command surface is `entire checkpoint sync` with a full non-interactive form (`--to`, `--from`, `--remove`, `--yes`, `--dry-run`, `--json`). |
| D2 | New election tier: a **sole** `entire://` remote is auto-elected after `config` and `observed`, before `origin`/sole/first. Source `SyncRemoteSourceEntire = "entire"`. |
| D3 | Scope: git-refs natively; git-branch repos are first **converted to git-refs** (existing `checkpoint.MigrateBranchToRefs`) and the primary flipped, then published to Entire. Dedicated `checkpoint_remote` repos are out of scope (explained, not migrated). |
| D4 | Removal from the old remote is opt-in, happens only after ls-remote verification that every artifact is on the Entire remote at the local hash, and is never implied by a bare non-interactive run. |

### 1.4 Migration engine: new `strategy/checkpoint_sync_migrate.go`

File header states: runs only from a foreground command, so `gitrepo.EnvWithoutRepoOverrides` is deliberately not applied (CLAUDE.md rule targets hook subprocesses); if ever wired into a hook, `remote.Fetch/PushWithOptions` do not scrub the environment.

```go
type ProgressFunc func(format string, args ...any)
type CheckpointInventory struct {
    Remote   string
    Refs     map[plumbing.ReferenceName]plumbing.Hash // refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<id>
    V1Branch plumbing.Hash                            // zero when absent
}
const migrateRemoteTimeout = checkpointRemoteForegroundFetchTimeout // 2 min per network step
const refChunkSize = 200                                            // refspecs per git invocation

func InventoryCheckpointArtifacts(ctx, remoteName string) (CheckpointInventory, error)
func HydrateCheckpointArtifacts(ctx, repo, from string, inv CheckpointInventory, progress ProgressFunc) (HydrateResult, error)
func RequeueAllCheckpointRefs(ctx, repo) (int, error)
func VerifyCheckpointArtifacts(ctx, repo, newRemote string, expected []plumbing.ReferenceName) (verified, missing []plumbing.ReferenceName, err error)
func RemoveCheckpointArtifacts(ctx, oldRemote string, refs []plumbing.ReferenceName, deleteV1 bool, progress ProgressFunc) (RemoveResult, error)
```

1. **Inventory**: `remote.LsRemoteInDir(ctx, worktreeRoot, remoteName, checkpoint.CheckpointRefPrefix+"*", "refs/heads/"+paths.MetadataBranchName)` by remote **name** (git applies insteadOf and dispatches the helper) under `migrateRemoteTimeout`. Move the parser into `checkpoint/refs_naming.go` as `ParseLsRemoteRefs(output) map[plumbing.ReferenceName]plumbing.Hash` plus `ParseCheckpointRefNames`; make `cli.parseCheckpointRefNames` a delegate.
2. **Hydrate**: candidates are inventory refs absent locally or at a different hash. Fetch in chunks with `remote.Fetch{Remote: from, RefSpecs: "+<ref>:refs/entire-sync-tmp/…", NoTags: true, NoFilter: true}` (NoFilter is mandatory, see `checkpoint_remote.go:169-181`), promote each with `SafelyAdvanceLocalRef` (not `PromoteTmpRefSafely`, which reopens the repo from cwd), remove the tmp ref. Same for the v1 branch onto `checkpoint.ResolveRefs(ctx).Primary`. Doc comment explains why this is the one sanctioned non-elected-remote advance: foreground, consented, the source is about to be deleted, and promotion is the same non-destructive primitive.
3. **Convert**: CLI calls `checkpoint.MigrateBranchToRefs(ctx, repo, false)` after hydrate whenever a local v1 branch exists (any backend). Nothing new in strategy.
4. **Requeue + publish**: `RequeueAllCheckpointRefs` iterates `repo.References()` keeping `checkpoint.ParseRef` hits, then `PushQueue.EnqueueAll(refs)` (new, one lock). Publish is existing `EnsureRedactionConfigured` + `PushQueuedCheckpointRefs(ctx, repo, newRemote)`. **Required fix**: chunk `batchPushRefs` at `refChunkSize` (`push_common.go:58-70`). Add `refsPushProgressWriter io.Writer = os.Stderr` (mirroring `opfPrePushProgressWriter`, `manual_commit_push.go:34`) and route the `[entire] Pushing …` line and dots (`:535-536`) through it so the CLI can silence them under its spinner.
5. **Verify**: one ls-remote of the new remote; a ref is verified iff present at the local hash.
6. **Remove**: new `remote.DeleteRefs(ctx, target, dir string, refs []string) (absent []string, err error)` in `checkpoint/remote/git.go` built on `PushWithOptions{ExtraArgs: ["--delete"]}`; on `remote ref does not exist`, re-ls-remote the chunk, drop absent names, retry once. Generalize `trail_cmd.go` `deleteBranchFromRemote` onto it. **Target is the old remote's push URL** (`gitremote.GetPushURLs`), never its name, to bypass `resolvePushCommandTarget`'s dedicated-repo rewrite; refuse a fan-out remote (>1 push URL). Chunk at `refChunkSize`; only verified refs. Delete `refs/heads/entire/checkpoints/v1` when asked and prune the stale local tracking ref `refs/remotes/<old>/entire/checkpoints/v1`.
7. Legacy read tier after removal needs no change: `FetchCheckpointRefFrom` treats the elected remote as authoritative and origin's absence as absence; nothing persists an "absent" verdict.

Engine ordering (CLI enforces): Inventory(old…) → Hydrate(all sources, refs + v1) → Convert (if local v1) → *backend flip* → Requeue → EnsureRedactionConfigured → Publish(new) → Verify(new) → Remove(old, verified only) → `MarkEntireSyncMigration`.

### 2.2 Command

`Use: "sync"`, `Short: "Move checkpoints to a single remote and bring older ones with them"`. Long explains the four steps (convert, fetch, push+verify, remove with consent), that the destination is the Entire remote when there is one, that `--to` records `strategy_options.checkpoint_push_remote` in `.entire/settings.local.json` because a remote name is a per-clone fact, and that without a terminal it reports and writes nothing unless `--yes`, deletes nothing unless `--remove`.

Flags: `--to <remote>`, `--from <remote>` (repeatable), `--remove`, `--yes` (never implies `--remove`), `--dry-run` (network reads only), `--json` (no prompts). `--dry-run` is mutually exclusive with `--remove` and `--yes`.

Runner: gather inputs (settings, election, `strategy.EntireRemotes`, raw remote list, dedicated-mode probe as `status.go:353`, backend + `ENTIRE_CHECKPOINTS_PRIMARY`, local checkpoint count, queue length, `push_sessions`, marker, `CanPromptInteractively`; inventory every non-destination remote and the destination unless the planner short-circuits) → plan → header → non-interactive/JSON without `--yes` prints plan + exact command and returns → execute with confirmations → celebration.

`--to` write (R2): `setCheckpointPushRemoteLocally` mirrors `enableExternalAgentsLocally` but edits the nested `strategy_options.checkpoint_push_remote` key via `settings.LoadLocalRaw`/`SaveLocalRaw`, then verifies by re-resolving the election (`Name == to && Source == config`); on failure print the tracked-local-file remedy (`git rm --cached .entire/settings.local.json`).

Backend flip: `updateCheckpointBackend(ctx, w, EnableOptions{CheckpointBackend: checkpointBackendRefsAlias})`, which writes the **project** file when present (a repo-wide format decision; a local-only flip would leave teammates recreating the v1 backlog; the local `checkpoints` block replaces the project one wholesale). Print `Commit .entire/settings.json so everyone writes the same store.` (omit when it landed in the local file). Skip and say so when `ENTIRE_CHECKPOINTS_PRIMARY` is set.

Prompts: confirmations via `confirmSyncStep` wrapping `confirmDoctorFix` (Ctrl+C and non-interactive read as decline). One combined confirmation for the non-destructive part, removal always its own question per old remote, naming count, v1 branch, and redacted URL: `Delete 128 checkpoint refs and the entire/checkpoints/v1 branch from origin (github.com/o/r)? Your code is untouched.` Pickers (states b, f, g) via `huh.NewSelect` in `NewAccessibleForm`; first option is always the no-change default (`Decide later (no change)` / current election / `Leave as is`) because accessible mode answers an unreadable prompt with the first option.

content.text:
The work is complete and verified. Nothing is committed; the changes sit in the working tree on `main` for you to review.

**What was wrong.** The multi-remote note in `remote_topology.go` and the git-refs multi-URL warning told users to set `checkpoint_remote`. That key is a `{provider, repo}` object for a dedicated GitHub checkpoint repository, so a remote name placed there was silently ignored. The real picker is `strategy_options.checkpoint_push_remote` in `.entire/settings.local.json`. Both strings are fixed and now pinned by tests.

**What was built.**

- **Entire tier in the election.** A sole `entire://` remote is auto-elected after an explicit setting or a captured election and before `origin`. Detection reads raw `.git/config` urls and pushurls, so `insteadOf` rewrites cannot hide or fake it, and a remote with any non-Entire URL never qualifies. Capture cannot displace it.
- **Pre-push follows the Entire remote.** Once elected, every `git push`, to any remote or raw URL, carries checkpoints to the Entire remote by name. The first delivery prints one stderr line, latched by a ledger file in the git common dir.
- **`entire checkpoint sync`.** A pure planner covers 15 named states. A bare non-interactive run reports the plan and the exact command and changes nothing. With consent it hydrates from the old remote, converts git-branch checkpoints to refs and flips the primary store, requeues, publishes through the OPF-gated queue, verifies every ref by ls-remote at its local hash, and only then, with `--remove` or a separate prompt, deletes from the old remote. The old remote is addressed by push URL so the dedicated-repo rewrite can never redirect a delete. Flags: `--to`, `--from`, `--remove`, `--yes`, `--dry-run`, `--json`.
- **The reward.** A closing block computed locally shows checkpoints, sessions, agents, tokens of agent work (with a new `M` suffix), and the date range, then what changes going forward. It never claims a removal that failed.
- **Surfaces.** `entire status` annotates the Entire remote, nudges toward the command while older checkpoints may remain elsewhere, and exposes `checkpoint_sync_migration` in JSON. `entire doctor` reports the destination when it is worth saying. Re-enable prints a pointer. README, CLAUDE.md and the architecture doc are updated.

**Verification.**

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `mise run lint` | 0 issues |
| `go test ./...` | pass |
| Integration suite, both backends | pass |
| Vogon E2E canary | 4/4 pass |

One caveat about the test runs: on this machine a global `insteadOf` rule rewrites GitHub HTTPS to SSH, which fails seven pre-existing URL-expectation tests regardless of this change. I ran everything with `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null` and saved a memory note about it.

**Two decisions you may want to revisit.** Every push now carries checkpoints to the Entire remote even when the push names GitHub. And the git-branch empty-remote defer is skipped under that redirect, which assumes the Entire server never adopts `entire/checkpoints/v1` as a mirror's default branch.
I want these committed (but not pushed!) in a toby/checkpoint-sync branch.
